Ratings track the 2026 NBL season through Week 11. The league, its teams and players are fictional parodies.

SINGLE GAME

In Handoff mode the CPU plays defense for both sides. When the ball changes hands, the game pauses so you can pass the device.

SETTINGS

Field view

Both views play from behind the offense, Blitz-style. Vertical is a tall portrait screen; horizontal is widescreen, held sideways. On a phone the game rotates to match.

Passing

Drag & release: pull back anywhere like a slingshot and let go. Receiver buttons: three Blitz-style buttons under your QB, ordered like your receivers line up. Tap one to throw, timed for when its receiver flashes green.

Difficulty
Quarter length
Sound
Replays
Broadcast FX
Light shows

The home crowd's touchdown light show: the lights round the top of the stadium go white, black out, then flash and chase in the team's colours. Calm keeps the colours but drops the fast strobes.

Score bug

Classic sits in the top-left corner. Broadcast is a TV network style, across the top in the middle: team boxes in team colours, the scores, the clock in the centre, timeouts as dashes and the down and distance on a flag under the team with the ball.

Coaching mode

Run the team from the sideline as head coach: your coordinators send in the plays and you approve or deny them. When this is on, you can turn coaching on for a season in Season Settings, or next to Home/Away when you pick a single game. On the sideline, the TIMEOUT button under your coordinators stops the clock whenever a timeout is allowed, and the camera button above them goes from your spot on the SIDELINE to the PLAY CAM to the PRESS BOX, where your coordinators watch from.

      HOW TO PLAY
      Receiver buttons (if set): three buttons under the QB, left to right in the same order the receivers line up. The matching symbol floats over each receiver; green means open. Keys 1–3.
      Drag passing: after the snap, press anywhere, pull back like a slingshot toward your own end, aim the yellow marker at a receiver, release to throw. Green rings are open receivers.
      Running: hold and drag anywhere to move; the middle ring is full speed, and pushing out to the dashed outer ring fires turbo. Runners cut on their own while getting through the line; HURDLE and DIVE sit on the left. Let go and your player keeps going on his own.
      Between plays: the offense huddles while the play is picked and the defense waits in its base set; once the call is in, the huddle breaks and everyone hustles to the line. Tap to snap any time; the ball goes the moment they're set. On defense you have 15 seconds to pick or the base defense (Cover 2) goes in. With the ball down in bounds the clock keeps running through all of it.
      Held sideways (Horizontal): steer with your left thumb anywhere on the field. Everything else is under your right thumb: a TURBO button to hold (the ring around it is what's left), DIVE beside it, HURDLE above it, and the three receiver buttons in the same spot when you throw.
      QB run: on a pass play, drag with a second finger while aiming (Drag & Release), or drag anywhere outside the three buttons (Receiver Buttons).
      Trick plays: Flea Flicker, HB Pass, Double Pass and Reverse are on pages 4 and 5; the throw unlocks once the ball has changed hands.
      Trucking: hit a tackler head-on while in turbo and you can run him over; a defender in turbo can flatten his blocker. Both burn turbo.
      Defense: tap a defender to take control, then drag to chase. Hurdle jumps to swat a pass. Dive lunges for the tackle.
      Team ratings: PASSING is how far the quarterback can throw (and how true the deep ones go), RUSHING how often the backs run through tackles, LINEMEN how long the pocket holds, DEFENSE how tight the coverage is, and SPECIAL TEAMS the extra point, the length of punts and how fast the kick coverage gets down the field.
      Keys: arrows/WASD move · Space turbo · I hurdle · K dive · Enter snap.
